expectations.evidence: Only VS-NfD is named and discussed. VS-VERTRAULICH, GEHEIM, and STRENG GEHEIM are never mentioned anywhere in the document.

Extensive detail on IT-Grundschutz: BSI-Standards 200-1 through 200-4 are explained, protection needs assessment (Schutzbedarfsfeststellung) at HOCH level discussed, Section 17 dedicated to implementation with modules, documentation requirements, and tooling (verinice).

Section 16 explains the full C5 attestation process: all 17 C5 domains listed with mappings, auditor selection (Wirtschaftspruefer), Type 1 vs Type 2 attestation explained, annual re-attestation, and Zusatzkriterien for government use.

Section 11 provides layer-by-layer analysis: BSI-approved products mandatory for cross-site VPN (SINA, genuscreen), HSMs (Utimaco CC EAL4+), and perimeter firewalls. FLOSS acceptable for internal firewalling, hypervisor, TLS, disk encryption with caveats. Key principle articulated clearly.

BSI TR-02102 (parts 2 and 3) and TR-03116 explicitly referenced. Specific algorithms listed: AES-256-GCM, ECDHE with brainpoolP256r1/brainpoolP384r1 (BSI preference over NIST curves), IKEv2 with specific DH groups. Section 8 covers full crypto architecture.

Section 12 dedicated to data sovereignty: all data including metadata/logs/backups within Germany, no foreign-entity access, German-national-only operations staff with security clearances, DSGVO/BDSG referenced in regulatory table, no foreign cloud dependencies.

Section 17 lists all applicable Bausteine by category (INF, SYS, NET, APP, OPS, DER, ISMS/ORP/CON) with specific module numbers. Section 17.2 covers Schutzbedarfsfeststellung. Section 17.3 lists all 8 mandatory documentation artifacts. Risk analysis per BSI-Standard 200-3 described. No explicit mention of the threat catalog (Gefaehrdungskatalog) by name, but methodology is thoroughly covered.

Section 11 provides a detailed layer-by-layer matrix of 15+ components with FLOSS possible/BSI required columns. Sections 11.2 and 11.3 give detailed justifications for why BSI approval is needed (crypto boundary crossing, tamper resistance) vs where FLOSS is acceptable (internal encryption with approved algorithms). Nuanced conditions stated.

Section 17.1 maps specific IT-Grundschutz modules to OpenStack components (SYS.1.5 Virtualisierung for KVM, SYS.1.3 for Linux, NET.3.2/3.3 for firewalls/VPN, APP.5.3 for cloud applications). Section 11.3 explains OpenStack is acceptable as the Gesamtsystem must meet Grundschutz, not individual components needing approval.
NIS2, EUCS are never mentioned. DSGVO/GDPR is referenced in the regulatory table but NIS2 and the EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme are absent. No broader EU regulatory context provided.

Section 15 provides a detailed 5-phase accreditation roadmap from ISMS setup through VS-NfD Freigabe to C5 Type 2 attestation, with a month-by-month timeline (18-30 months total). Phase 5 explicitly covers ongoing operations: annual IT-Grundschutz review, annual C5 re-attestation, continuous monitoring.

German standards are primary throughout: BSI IT-Grundschutz, BSI C5, BSI TRs, VSA, BDSG/DSGVO. US standards (FIPS, DISA STIG, CIS) mentioned only as supplementary references. Architecture centers on German-approved products (SINA, genuscreen, Utimaco) and German sovereignty requirements.
